thread:
pagerbot: PAGER: auth-service high 5xx+auth-fail spike detected (cluster: prod-auth, region: us-west-2). Pager duty: @maria on-call.

maria: On it. Looking at the alert — attaching short dump.

maria: quick grep shows a ~10k increase in 401s from a small set of IPs. Also seeing repeated `x-auth-session` header in logs with apparently plaintext tokens.

ken: Uh — are these from a staging forwarder or prod?

maria: prod. Indexer stream shows request_id 0a3f... repeated from IPs 18.212.45.9, 52.24.33.100.

lex: I see matching entries in the observability pipeline where a debug logger leaked headers during a retry backoff. Likely a config flip on auth-proxy.

irene: If headers leaked to logs, we need to assume token exposure. Recommend immediate rotate of service tokens and ephemeral session revocation.

maria: Agreed. Taking these steps now: 1) throttling the source IPs at edge WAF, 2) temporary disable debug header logging, 3) start token revocation.

maria: WAF rule pushed: `block ip 18.212.45.9/32,52.24.33.100/32` (testing). Will promote to rate-limit if false positives.

ken: How do we rotate service tokens without breaking jobs? Which scope keys?

irene: Rotate the auth-proxy service token first (scope: auth:proxy). Create new token, update proxy pools, then roll user session revocation job to scrub in-flight sessions older than 15m.

maria: Running rotate script on prod-keymgr now: `./rotate_key.sh --service auth-proxy --new` — leaving old token live for 3m for drain.

security-oncall: Heads up — we should snapshot S3 access logs and preserve for forensics before any scrub.

maria: Done. Snapshotted s3://redwood-prod-logs/auth-proxy/ to tmp forensic bucket `forensic-3350000123`.

lex: I pushed a patch to disable `log.headers` for the proxy in the feature flag service — will flip in 30s.

maria: Flag flipped. Confirming no further header dumps in the tail.

maria: Start session revocation job: `python tools/revoke_sessions.py --filter leaked=true --age_gt 0m` (this will revoke sessions that match leaked tokens).

ken: Noted. I’ll coordinate with infra to warm the new tokens into the cluster to avoid 502s.

irene: Customer impact assessment: initial checks show 0 customer-facing errors, just auth noise. But treat as potential credential exposure. Prepare a minimal notice template for CSM/legal if required.

security-oncall: Please also rotate any long-lived API keys referenced in the forensic snapshot. Make a list and tag owners.

maria: Generating key ownership list from snapshot now. Posting to the incident ticket when ready.

lex: One follow-up: add an automated alert rule to detect header-logging flips in staging so we catch config drift earlier.

maria: Agreed. I’ll add a low-severity detector and a runbook entry.

ken: handoff: I need to sleep in 30m; @lex please pick up live mitigation and verify token rotation fully propagated.

lex: Got it. I’ll monitor for 30m and then hand to security-oncall for longer-term forensics.

security-oncall: Acknowledged. Will start triage template: evidence catalog, affected keys, timeline, and decide on external comms.

maria: Summary (for the ticket): "debug header logging caused plaintext auth tokens to be written to prod logs; WAF blocked suspicious IPs; rotated auth-proxy token; revoked exposed sessions; snapshot taken for forensics; follow-up: rotate any long-lived keys found, postmortem and runbook update."

lex: small note — no sign of lateral access or S3 writes from those IPs beyond read attempts. Good sign.

security-oncall: Thanks all. Leaving this in "active investigation" and will update SOC timeline. If anyone finds affected customer tokens, escalate and draft comms.

maria: Closing immediate mitigation. Monitoring for 2h. Will update ticket with key list and timelines. :white_check_mark:
